newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end mixed in year's final session.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end mixed in year's final session.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed a bullish 1996 with a mixed tally Monday and were seen firm when trading resumes Thursday, dealers said.

"It was a pretty flat day, with prices caught in narrow bands as everyone expected," said Emilio Alessandro at brokers Alessandro. "However, the bolsa's slight negative bias was fading towards the end of the session and we might see stocks switch back into positive territory Thursday."
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.1 percent to 649.37, showing a 25 percent gain for 1996. Last Friday it closed at 650.23, the year's record high.
"The market was in a festive mood today -- everyone celebrated the end of a successful year and welcomed 1997," said Alessandro, describing the cheerful environment on the trading floor.
Traders noted the slack pace of trading mirrored little action in the foreign markets.
"Dealing everywhere is grinding to a halt ahead of the New Year," said another trader. "Here many players took the day off and for those who stayed in town it was a good time to take some profits."
Floor volume shrank by slightly more than half since Friday to 12 million pesos, while over-the-counter volume dwindled to 25.4 million pesos from 72.6 million on Friday.
The broad market index closed up 0.1 percent, with winners edging out losers 24 to 19 and 23 issues closing flat.
The day's top main-tier performers were construction stock Polledo, steelmaker Siderca and carmaker Ciadea, which tacked on 2.0 percent, 1.7 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively.
MerVal losses were led by petrochemical concerns Ipako and Indupa, which slid 2.5 percent and 1.7 percent each.
